name: reference-heavy-mkdocs-site
query: Review this MkDocs documentation for a developer-facing GitHub Action. The nav has Home, Actions Reference, Schemas, and Contributing. Give me the highest-impact improvements.
expected_behavior: Inspects the actual landing/reference content before assuming pages are missing
Evaluates first-success, common-task, reference, and troubleshooting journeys
Identifies task-oriented guidance as a likely gap when evidence supports it
Suggests a compact revised navigation rather than creating taxonomy for its own sake

name: documentation-code-drift
query: Review the docs and action.yml. The docs say input 'mode' defaults to deploy, but action.yml defaults it to template.
expected_behavior: Treats action.yml as a source of truth for the Action input
Reports the mismatch as a high or critical correctness issue depending on impact
Explains the user impact and names the exact smallest fix
Checks for the stale default in examples and other reference pages

name: good-small-project
query: Review a small MkDocs project whose index page contains a complete quickstart, actions.md is exhaustive and generated from metadata, schemas.md is source-derived, and troubleshooting is a section on index.md because there are only three common errors.
expected_behavior: Does not insist on separate pages merely to match a framework
Rewards concise information architecture that serves the reader journeys
Focuses on actual correctness, findability, and maintenance evidence

name: mkdocs-build-quality-gate
query: Review mkdocs.yml and docs CI. Several internal links are stale, a nav entry points to a renamed file, and CI runs mkdocs build without strict mode.
expected_behavior: Identifies the broken navigation and links as concrete defects
Recommends using the project-compatible strict/link validation mechanism
Does not install or upgrade dependencies during a review without permission
Separates current breakage from longer-term toolchain maintenance recommendations
